rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable heart failure from wheeze/tight chest
rule_level_problems.problem: The page gives two independent routes to 'heart failure likely'; only the orthopnoea-and-leg-swelling route is encoded. The second route (age ≥ 50 with a first episode of wheeze/tight chest) cannot be written because the grammar has no numeric age, but nothing in the file records that this branch was dropped, and a patient over 50 with first-episode wheeze and no leg swelling will get no heart failure prompt at all. 'First episode' exists as a SNOMED qualifier value, so the only blocker is age.

rule_level_problems.rule: Emergency: life-threatening wheeze/tight chest; Urgent: severe wheeze/tight chest
rule_level_problems.problem: Pulse is compared on 'Pulse, function' (8499008) and saturation on 'Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen' (103228002). SNOMED also has 'Heart rate' (364075005) and 'Peripheral oxygen saturation' (431314004), which are the usual observables for a pulse and a pulse-oximeter reading. Whether these clauses ever fire depends on which concept the vitals system records; I could not verify that from the permitted inputs. If the system records the other concept, pulse < 50, pulse > 120 and SpO2 < 90% are silently dead.

The page labels this branch 'Life threatening' and its management 'Refer urgently', the same words as the Severe branch; it never says 'emergency'. Emergency is a reasonable reading of the escalation above Severe but is a judgment the house standard asks to be explicit about.

'If first episode of wheeze/tight chest, assess for asthma and COPD' has no possible Asthma / COPD rule, although 'First episode' (qualifier value) and 'Asthma' (disorder) exist. Low consequence given the cross-reference to the asthma/COPD page.

The one-hour reassessment branch (talk normally, RR < 20 vs ≥ 20, PEFR improved by > 20%, worsening → manage as severe) is not modelled. This is a language limit (no treatment state, no change-over-time), and the worsening branch would not raise priority above the existing Urgent, so no triage outcome is lost; worth recording as could-not-model.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from sudden wheeze/tight chest
rule_level_problems.problem: Allergen exposure is not bounded to 'within the past few hours'; an old recorded exposure could satisfy the rule. Minor, as the rule is a possible pre-screen and the gold standard page 20 takes the same approach.

summary: The red box is encoded faithfully: all twelve life-threatening and severe criteria are present with correct thresholds, directions and or-logic, silent chest follows the page's own definition, and the baseline 'urgent attention' is an Urgent rule. The most consequential gap is the second heart-failure route (age ≥ 50 with first-episode wheeze/tight chest), which the grammar cannot express and the file does not acknowledge. The pulse and saturation clauses use 'Pulse, function' and 'Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen' rather than 'Heart rate' and 'Peripheral oxygen saturation', so whether they fire depends on which concept the vitals system records.
